newsitem.title: USA: Study calls for campaign reforms in Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Study calls for campaign reforms in Illinois.

text.p: In a report that echoes the national debate on campaign financing, a bi-partisan task force said on Wednesday money flowing to some Illinois politicians had poisoned the system.
"It does not matter who is in power. These are institutional problems that are exploited by members of both parties," former U.S. senator Paul Simon said.

Simon, a Democrat, headed the task force along with former Illinois governor William Stratton, a Republican. Its report said one major problem was that big money was concentrated in the hands of the majority and minority leaders of the state House and Senate.
The current system was "so out of control that our lifeblood, democracy, is tainted," the report said.

The study recommended limits on contributions to candidates and on transfers of funds from committees controlled by legislative leaders, as well as the establishment of a permanent campaign finance commission to monitor the flow of political contributions.

"Wealthy contributors use our democratic process to add to their power and wealth. Citizens increasingly feel left out and under-represented by their own elected officials, and they feel powerless to change the system," the report said.

It recommended that contributions from individuals, groups and corporations in the state be limited to $2,000 per election and that transfers from political committees and parties have $25,000 caps for primaries and general elections.
It also said campaign funds in excess of $25,000 should not be carried over after an election.
